auto_merge.commit_title: gh-146011: Fix use-after-free in `signaldict_repr` after deletion (#153784)

files.patch:
@@ -4147,6 +4147,15 @@ def test_float_operation_default(self):
 @requires_cdecimal
 class CContextFlags(ContextFlags, unittest.TestCase):
     decimal = C
+
+    def test_signaldict_repr(self):
+        Context = self.decimal.Context
+        ctx = Context(prec=7)
+        mapping = ctx.flags
+        del ctx
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'invalid signal dict'):
+            repr(mapping)
+
 class PyContextFlags(ContextFlags, unittest.TestCase):
     decimal = P

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+Fix a heap-use-after-free in the C implementation of :mod:`decimal`
+when calling :func:`repr` after deleting the :class:`~decimal.Context`.

review_comments.body:
This will introduce a memory leak, if context was not deleted before.  You miss DECREF in this case, no?

I think that my suggestion in the issue thread is more correct.
I'm not sure if I understand exactly. `traps->flags` contains a borrowed reference so even if the context object is not freed beforehand, there is no memory leak.
It's not obvious that traps or flags can survive after context_dealloc(), it would be useful to add a comment to explain it with a reference to the issue (gh-146011).

 context_clear(PyObject *op)
 {
     PyDecContextObject *self = _PyDecContextObject_CAST(op);
+    /* Since traps and flags hold a borrowed reference to the
+       flags stored in the context object, these references need
+       to be cleared when the context object is deallocated
+       because other objects could hold references to the
